newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus inists on HIV sufferer's right to school.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus inists on HIV sufferer's right to school.

text.p: Cyprus's health and education ministers have intervened to make sure a child tested HIV positive will go to school without harassment from parents of other children, officials said on Wednesday.

Parents of toddlers in a government-run nursery at a village in the Famagusta region in the island's southeast have threatened to take their children to other schools if the four-year-old tested HIV positive is taken there.
The boy, who contracted the human immunodeficiency virus at birth, is due to go to Britain soon for medical tests. He is due to start preschool at the village in January.

"The child will start school whenever it wants. Nobody can stop it," education ministry representative Argyris Constantinou told Reuters. "We are making every effort to convince them they have to accept this child."
The education ministry provides HIV children with 'minders' at school for their protection and the protection of other children, he added.
The education and health ministers will visit the community next week and talk to parents.

"The child was asked what present he wanted at Christmas and he said he wanted to go to school," Health Minister Manolis Christofides told Sigma, a private Cypriot television channel, on Tuesday night.
"He asked for the simplest of things, and nobody has the right to deny him this," Christofides added.
